title: Rapid prototype usability sessions — June 2026 synthesis
content:
Purpose and scope:
Run 6 rapid usability sessions against the low-fidelity console prototype (model selection, route creation, rollout config, and simple cost/latency dashboard). Goal: identify key friction for first-time and returning engineers and convert findings into high-impact backlog items for the next sprint.

Participants and roles:
- 6 participants total (3 external customers via recruitment firm, 3 internal: solutions eng + recent hire dev).
- Moderator: Aisha Patel
- Note-taker: Miguel Santos
- Prototype owner / observer: Priya Narang
- Engineering SME on-call: Evan Zhou

Protocol summary:
- Think-aloud tasks (4 tasks, ~20–25 minutes per session) + 5-minute SUS-style quick survey at end.
- Tasks targeted: 1) create a new route pinned to a Redwood-hosted model variant; 2) configure rollout: canary -> 25% -> auto-roll; 3) enable KV caching for a route and preview estimated cost impact; 4) diagnose a slow request using tracing panel.
- Prototype fidelity: low fidelity Figma with interactive hotspots; no real data.

High-level takeaways (synthesis):
1) Mental model mismatch on "route" vs "endpoint" — 5/6 users expected "endpoint" language. Confusion caused hesitation when creating routes.
2) Rollout UX: canary flow is understood conceptually but the UI makes it hard to specify kickback criteria (percentages ok, but no linked metrics to evaluate success). Users wanted pre-built metric templates (latency spike, error rate).
3) Cost preview is valuable but felt opaque: users wanted token-count estimates for recent prompts or representative traffic, not just a % delta.
4) Tracing panel overwhelmed first-time users — too many tabs and cryptic terms (KV cache hit ratio, p99 warmup). Users wanted a "quick triage" CTA that surfaces the top 2 likely causes.
5) Discoverability: model catalog filters (by family, size, quantization) were buried; users often created routes without checking model variance/cost tradeoffs.

Representative quotes (verbatim):
- "I don't know what a route is — I just want an endpoint I can call from my app."
- "If I could pick 'latency regression' and the console auto-suggests a canary rollout with an alert rule, that'd be sweet."
- "The cost graph is pretty, but tell me how many tokens per minute I'm paying for — even ballpark."

Quantitative signals (quick numbers):
- Task success rate: 83% overall (5/6 completed all tasks).
- Median task time: 7:30 (create route), 9:10 (configure rollout), 6:40 (enable caching), 11:20 (diagnose trace).
- SUS-style quick rating: median 72 (ok but room to polish).

Wireframe-specific feedback (by screen):
- Model selection modal: add short labels for "cost tier" and default to showing estimated request cost for 1k tokens. Also add a secondary label for "suitable for chat/generation/embedding".
- Route creation: change header copy from "New Route" to "Create endpoint (route)" and add microcopy explaining route vs API key.
- Rollout editor: add "metric templates" dropdown and an inline preview of how the selected metric will evaluate the canary over a 1-hour window (synthetic example).
- Cost preview modal: provide both % delta and absolute token estimate + monthly projection based on recent hourly estimate.
- Tracing/diagnostics: introduce a "Quick Triage" collapsed card that shows top 3 signals (high p99, cache miss surge, model variant fallback) and suggested first actions.

Accessibility & copy notes:
- Some color contrast issues in the heatmap legend — flag to design.
- Avoid jargon: replace "KV" with "context cache (KV)" on first mention.

Backlog grooming output (prioritized list with rationale):
1) RW-1902 - Rename route header + microcopy update (low effort, high clarity). Priority: P0 for next sprint. Owner: Priya. Est: 1 dev day + copy review.
2) RW-1903 - Add metric templates to rollout editor (medium effort). Priority: P0. Owner: Evan + Product. Est: 3–4 dev days + telemetry wiring.
3) RW-1904 - Cost preview: add token estimate and monthly projection (medium effort). Priority: P1. Owner: Product + Billing. Est: 3 dev days.
4) RW-1905 - Quick Triage card in tracing panel (higher effort: requires engineering rules). Priority: P1. Owner: SRE/Observability. Est: 5 dev days.
5) RW-1906 - Model catalog UI: surface cost tier and use-case labels (low effort). Priority: P2. Owner: Design + Product. Est: 2 dev days.
6) RW-1907 - Accessibility: contrast fixes and copy updates for jargon (very low effort). Priority: P2. Owner: Design. Est: 1 dev day.

Risks and open questions:
- Telemetry availability: rollout metric templates require a consistent metric infra; confirm with observability whether synthetic preview windows are feasible without production metrics. (Blocked: ask SRE — linked ticket RW-1910)
- Cost model alignment: billing team needs to approve token estimate logic to avoid mismatch with invoices. (Next: sync with Billing on RW-1904)
- Language/terminology decision across console: if we switch to "endpoint" everywhere, we need to map existing docs/SDKs. Suggest doc-only change first, then broader rename once customers confirm.

Next steps / action items (owners and dates):
- Priya: implement microcopy + header change mockups and push Figma update by 2026-06-21. (Action)
- Evan: scope telemetry needs for metric templates; sync with SRE by 2026-06-18. (Action)
- Miguel: convert recorded session clips into 6 highlight clips for stakeholders and upload to the folder by 2026-06-19. (Action)
- Aisha: draft a short customer email summarizing planned improvements and invite feedback from the 3 external participants by 2026-06-22. (Action)

Appendix (notes from individual sessions):
- Session 1 (external dev): got stuck on route vs endpoint naming; suggested default name templates.
- Session 2 (external dev): loved the idea of metric templates; wanted an "error ratio > 0.5%" template.
- Session 3 (internal): struggled to find model family filter; suggested persistent sidebar filters.
- Session 4 (external dev): asked for sample cURL snippet next to route create for quick copy-paste.
- Session 5 (internal): suggested combining cost preview with rollout editor to show cost impact per variant.
- Session 6 (external dev): wanted a single-click rollback option in rollout history.

Files in this folder: Figma prototype link, session recordings, quick spreadsheet with raw times (see linked artifacts).

Summary sentence to share with execs:
6 quick sessions revealed a set of low-effort, high-impact fixes (language clarifications, microcopy, cost estimate visibility) plus 2 medium-effort initiatives (metric templates and a quick-triage diagnostics card) that should materially reduce first-time friction and support safer canary rollouts."
